en: The Philippines consists of exactly 7,641 islands, which is over 500 more islands than the previously accepted count of 7,107.
Mount Apo stands at 2,954 meters tall, which is nearly three times higher than Mount Makiling's elevation of 1,090 meters.
Mayon Volcano has erupted over 50 times in the last 400 years, making it the most active volcano in the Philippines.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers from the Caraballo Mountains to the sea.
Lake Taal is the deepest lake in the Philippines, reaching 172 meters deep, which is much deeper than Laguna de Bay.
The Sierra Madre mountain range stretches about 540 kilometers along eastern Luzon, making it the longest mountain range in the country.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features an 8.2-kilometer underground river, which is one of the longest navigable underground rivers in the world.
The Philippine Trench drops to a maximum depth of 10,540 meters, making it the third deepest oceanic trench globally.
Baguio City receives an average annual rainfall of about 4,000 millimeters, which is double the national average of 2,000 millimeters.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of at least 1,268 symmetrical mounds spread across an area of more than 50 square kilometers.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park covers a total marine area of 97,030 hectares, protecting a massive and highly biodiverse coral ecosystem.
The 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo ejected about 10 cubic kilometers of material, making it the second-largest volcanic eruption of the twentieth century.
